description:
The image displays two ground-level photographs of agricultural landscapes illustrating different land cover types relevant for land use / land cover (LULC) classification.
The left photograph shows a field of mown or harvested grassland, characterized by dry, yellowish-brown stubble and distinct parallel tracks, likely from mowing or harvesting machinery. A small pink marker is visible on the ground in the foreground. A line of trees and buildings is visible on the horizon.
The right photograph depicts a field of standing golden-yellow cereal crops (arable land) under a blue sky with scattered white clouds. A green, uncultivated strip, possibly a path or field margin, runs between the main crop field on the left and a strip of tall, dry grasses and a hedgerow on the right. A single tree is visible in the distance above the hedgerow.
These images visually distinguish between managed grasslands (or recently harvested fields) and active arable land, alongside areas of unmanaged vegetation, which is pertinent for methods like CORINE Land Cover (CLC) class 2.3.1 (Pastures) and for discriminating permanent grasslands from arable land. A faint, unreadable text string is present at the bottom left of the left image.
